takeaway: The facial nerve gives taste, not general sensation, to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue; CN IX supplies the posterior third. So the sensation statement is false.

question.text: Which statement about the anatomy of the facial nerve is NOT true?
question.say: Which statement about the anatomy of the facial nerve is not true?

answer.text: It supplies sensation to the posterior two-thirds of the tongue.
answer.say: It supplies sensation to the posterior two-thirds of the tongue.

lines.text: The facial nerve leaves the skull through the stylomastoid foramen.
It supplies the muscles of facial expression, including the platysma, and the stapedius in the ear.
It also gives parasympathetic supply to the sublingual gland.
On the tongue, it carries taste from the anterior two-thirds.
Sensation to the posterior third of the tongue comes from the glossopharyngeal nerve, CN IX.
lines.say: Sensation to the posterior third of the tongue comes from the glossopharyngeal nerve, cranial nerve nine.

lines.text: So the facial nerve does not give sensation to the posterior tongue, and that statement is false.
